nl: A worker started as `tools/worker.py bench-worker-4` (PID in run/worker.pid) is running. It stops cleanly when the file run/stop exists. Ask it to stop this way and wait until it has exited.

entries.content_utf8:
import os
import pathlib
import signal
import sys
import time

pathlib.Path("run").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
pathlib.Path("logs").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
log = open("logs/worker.log", "a")


def stop(*_):
    log.write("stopped cleanly\n")
    log.flush()
    pathlib.Path("run/worker.pid").unlink(missing_ok=True)
    sys.exit(0)


signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
log.write(f"started {sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'normal'}\n")
log.flush()
pathlib.Path("run/worker.pid").write_text(str(os.getpid()))
while True:
    if pathlib.Path("run/stop").exists():
        stop()
    time.sleep(0.1)

setup.description: tools/worker.py runs in the background and has written run/worker.pid.
setup.bash:
setsid python3 tools/worker.py bench-worker-4 > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null &
for i in $(seq 100); do [ -s run/worker.pid ] && break; sleep 0.1; done

touch run/stop
until grep -q 'stopped cleanly' logs/worker.log; do sleep 0.1; done
while pgrep -f -- 'worker.py bench-worker-4' > /dev/null; do sleep 0.1; done
